newsitem.title: USA: Coleman owners to redeem notes, LYONS.
newsitem.headline: Coleman owners to redeem notes, LYONS.

text.p: Entities controlling 83 percent of Colemen Co Inc's common stock said Monday they will redeem notes with a face value of $281.3 million and retire LYONS -- Liquid Yield Option notes -- convertible into Colemen common.

In a joint statement, Coleman Holdings Inc and Coleman Worldwide Corp said Coleman Holdings intends to redeem its Senior Secured Discount Notes due 1998 by July 15 and Coleman Worldwide intends to retire its LYONS due 2013.
The notes and LYONS are backed by the 83 percent of Coleman owned by McAndrews & Forbes, spokesman Greg Woodland explained.

He said the firm will be forming a new holding company that will issue debt to fund the note redemption and LYONS retirement. Terms of that new offer will be available in about 24 hours he said late Tuesday.
Following the redemption and retirement, Woodland said, Coleman Holdings and Coleman Worldwide will be merged with the new company, simplifying the existing capital structure.
In Tuesday's statement, Coleman Worldwide said it will offer to pay cash for the LYONs in excess of the market value of the LYONS, which is based on the market value of 15.7 Coleman Co common shares.
Each $1,000 face value LYON is convertible into 15.7 million shares since the company's last two-for-one stock split, Woodland said. They are now trading for about $320 each.

Coleman Worldwide expects to start the offer as soon as reasonably practicable and redeem any remaining LYONs on May 27. Woodland expects the tender terms to be announced in about two weeks when the financing is concluded.
